name: Invisible Green
lede: Invisible green is a very dark green, named for how close it sits to black.

sections.title: A green you nearly cannot see
sections.body:
Paterson defines invisible green as a very dark green, called that because it verges on black [1].

Paterson's index files it among the greens, near names like [[ivy-green]] and [[malachite-green]] [2]. It also appears as one entry in a chart of named paint shades that Baty reproduces, alongside names such as Cassel Earth and Mars Black [3]. In that company it sits among the near-blacks [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here, #39615C, is a deep teal-leaning green that is lighter than the dictionary description suggests [4]. Treat it as one screen reading of the name; the books give no hex, and the dictionary's own wording points to something darker still [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The books say little more. We found no usable archive measurements for this name, so there are no painting statistics to quote [4]. Compare it with [[black-green]] and [[dark-green]], which sit in the same neighborhood [4].
